long_biography.plain_text:
For Troy Link, learning the meat-snack business began on the slaughterhouse floor. He worked in production before moving into sales and marketing, where he challenged the idea that customers would not pay more for bagged jerky. When his father questioned the launch cost, Troy devised a limited range of flavours and pack sizes. Resealable bags subsequently won shelf space at Walmart and Target.

Later, shortages exposed a different problem: the business could not make enough to serve its customers. Troy responded by committing to new factories, automation and expanded jerky production. He chose to add capacity ahead of demand rather than repeatedly leave retailers without stock.
